description: Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd, goes to look for treasure at the Pyramids. Coelho tells the story of the quest for self that has become a global phenomenon.

hero.hook: When you want something, the whole universe conspires: the phrase that has won over 65 million readers.

blocks.text: Published in **1988**,  is a global phenomenon: more than **65 million copies** sold, translated into 80 languages. The original title in Portuguese is *O Alquimista*. **Paulo Coelho**, born in **1947**, tells the story of the quest of a young Andalusian shepherd. It crystallizes the aspirations for self-realization specific to the end of the 20th century. [[The Alchemist]]

Initially unnoticed, with 900 copies in the first printing, the novel has become a manifesto of accessible wisdom. He redefines the relationships between spirituality, literature and commercial success. Its simple tone and universal lessons make it one of the most translated books in history.

Before his fame, **Paulo Coelho** was a lyricist for the Brazilian rocker , an emblematic figure of Brazilian rock of the 1970s. He turned to writing after a pilgrimage to  in **1986**. This experience marks a spiritual turning point in his life. [[Raul Seixas]] [[Santiago de Compostela]]

blocks.caption: Paulo Coelho, from editorial failure to the Guinness record for translations.

blocks.text: In **1988**, a small Brazilian publisher only printed 900 copies and refused to reprint. Coelho recovers his rights and finds , a publishing house which launches global success. [[Rocco]]

Personalities like Bill Clinton and Pharrell Williams have claimed that the book transformed their view of the world. He thus entered the , a dominant cultural movement which appeals to the greatest number of people. [[mainstream culture]]

sections.title: Coelho's trajectory and the editorial miracle

blocks.text: **Santiago**, Andalusian shepherd, dreams of a treasure at the **Pyramids** of Egypt. **Melchizedek**, the King of Salem, teaches him the **personal legend**. It is the destiny that everyone desires to achieve since childhood, often forgotten with age. He gives him two stones to read the signs.

blocks.caption: The Pyramids: the apparent goal of Santiago's journey.

blocks.text: Picked up in , a Moroccan port town where Santiago disembarks, he works for a crystal merchant. Then he crosses the  with a caravan. He meets **Fatima**, the love he agrees to leave to pursue his quest, and the **Alchemist**, who teaches him to read the signs of the universe. [[Tangier]] [[Sahara]]

sections.title: The journey of Santiago: an initiatory quest

blocks.text: The novel is based on the **Soul of the World**: everything that exists shares a unique energy, a language that the pure of heart can understand. “When you want something, the whole universe conspires to give it to you” sums up this optimistic vision of destiny.

The philosophy is **syncretic**, a mixture of traditions: biblical ethics, Islamic destiny with , “it was written”, Arabic expression of predestination, medieval alchemy transformed into psychological metaphor. This simplicity explains the massive public support, but also the criticism from academics who see it as naive optimism. [[Maktub]]

sections.title: The Soul of the World and philosophical syncretism

blocks.text: At the Pyramids, Santiago finds nothing. A thief tells him he dreamed of treasure under a sycamore tree in Spain, exactly where Santiago was sleeping at the beginning. The treasure was close, but the journey was necessary for Santiago to learn to listen to his heart.

Experience, Fatima and listening to the heart are worth more than gold. The book paved the way for 's fiction, literature aimed at realizing one's potential. This hybrid genre now dominates a large part of the publishing market. Coelho draws on the initiatory tale, the Bible and Sufism to offer universal wisdom, accessible to all readers. [[personal development]]
transforms a traditional tale into a life manual, going from 900 copies to a worldwide success based on personal legend and the quest for oneself. [[The Alchemist]]
